the identification and validation of novel immunohistochemical biomarkers for the diagnosis of Ewing Sarcoma.

the identification of new biomarkers for the diagnosis of cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BCL11B is a robust and reliable marker for Ewing sarcomas.

the expression of BCL-11b and GLG1 is a robust and reliable marker to confirm Ewing sarcoma, and that this can be done by IHC in a fast, simple, and cost efficient manner, and without the need for molecular diagnostics.
the expression of the EWSR1 fusion gene product, FLI1, is not only a hallmark of the disease but also a diagnostic tool to identify Ewing sarcomas in the absence of molecular diagnostics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified three novel diagnostic markers for Ewing Sarcoma.
we provide evidence that BCL11B (B-cell leukemia/lymphoma 11B) and GLG1 (glycerol-3-phosphate acyltransferase 1) are novel diagnostic markers for Ewing’s sarcoma.
the expression levels of ATP1A1, BCL11B, and GLG1 can be detected in formalin-fixed, paraffin embedded Ewing sarcoma tissue sections by IHC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EWSR1 fusion protein is a powerful transcription factor that drives the expression of a set of genes that can be detected by immunohistochemsitry (IHC).
the EWSR1 fusion partners are not only responsible for the oncogenic transformation, but also for the expression of a large number of downstream targets that can be used for diagnosis.
the identification of EWSR1-driven targets can lead to the discovery of robust diagnostic markers.
